title: Benign tubular adenoma polyp
notice: Synthetic and AI-written. Needs review by a pathologist before being used to score anything (issue #22).

keys.span: a benign polyp, but it could slowly turn into cancer over years if it were left alone
keys.correct: A tubular adenoma is a benign precancerous polyp that can slowly progress to cancer over years if not removed.
keys.source_hint: US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: Dysplasia means the cells look abnormal under the microscope.
keys.issue: Doesn't say that dysplasia is a precancerous change, or that high-grade dysplasia is the step closest to cancer.
keys.correct: Dysplasia is a precancerous change in the lining cells. Low-grade dysplasia is the usual finding in an adenoma; high-grade dysplasia is a more advanced change, closer to cancer.
keys.source_hint: CAP colon and rectum protocol; WHO classification of digestive system tumours
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: Once an adenoma has been removed completely, there's no need for another colonoscopy.
keys.issue: Surveillance colonoscopy is still recommended after an adenoma is removed.
keys.correct: Surveillance colonoscopy is still recommended. For one or two tubular adenomas under 10 mm, the next one is usually in 7 to 10 years.
keys.source_hint: US Multi-Society Task Force 2020 post-polypectomy surveillance
keys.speaker: doctor
